modernSources.citation: Thomas K, Peeler J. A Detailed Anatomical Description of the Gastrocnemius Muscle—Is It Anatomically Positioned to Function as an Antagonist to the Anterior Cruciate Ligament? Anatomia. 2024;3(4):244–255. DOI: 10.3390/anatomia3040021.
modernSources.edition: Journal article, volume 3 issue 4 (2024); publisher page published 2024-10-16.
modernSources.locator: Methods §2.2; Discussion §4.4. Publisher full text opened.
modernSources.accessMethod: Publisher full HTML, methods and discussion inspected.
modernSources.originResult: Supports a broad proximal attachment at the posterior-superior lateral femoral condyle; no reproducible boundary on the project femur mesh.
modernSources.insertionResult: The selected study focuses on the proximal gastrocnemius; it does not provide a distal calcaneal footprint comparable to the Gray insertion summary.

modernSources.citation: Bolsterlee B, Finni T, D’Souza A, Eguchi J, Clarke EC, Herbert RD. Three-dimensional architecture of the whole human soleus muscle in vivo. PeerJ. 2018;6:e4610. DOI: 10.7717/peerj.4610.
modernSources.edition: PeerJ volume 6, article e4610 (2018); publisher page published 2018-04-18.
modernSources.locator: Abstract, Methods and Results. Full article HTML opened.
modernSources.originResult: The study measures soleus architecture, not a tibial/fibular origin footprint; any anatomical descriptions in its background are context, not a new attachment measurement.
modernSources.insertionResult: It does not quantify the Gray-described shared Achilles/calcaneal insertion footprint.

modernSources.citation: Kimata K, Otsuka S, Yokota H, Shan X, Hatayama N, Naito M. Relationship between attachment site of tibialis anterior muscle and shape of tibia: anatomical study of cadavers. Journal of Foot and Ankle Research. 2022;15:54. DOI: 10.1186/s13047-022-00559-y.
modernSources.edition: Journal article, volume 15, article 54 (2022); version of record published 2022-07-12.
modernSources.locator: Methods and Results, tibial attachment site; publisher HTML full text opened.
modernSources.accessMethod: Springer Nature publisher full HTML inspected.
modernSources.originResult: Direct cadaveric measurements support a broad tibial origin and sex-related distal endpoint variation; the measured longitudinal endpoint is not a 2D footprint boundary.
modernSources.insertionResult: The medial cuneiform/first metatarsal insertion is described as background and cites prior work; this study does not experimentally measure that insertion.

modernSources.citation: Willegger M, Seyidova N, Schuh R, Windhager R, Hirtler L. The tibialis posterior tendon footprint: an anatomical dissection study. Journal of Foot and Ankle Research. 2020;13:25. DOI: 10.1186/s13047-020-00392-1.
modernSources.edition: Journal article, volume 13, article 25 (2020); version of record published 2020-05-19.
modernSources.locator: Methods and Results, distal tendon footprints; publisher HTML full text opened.
modernSources.accessMethod: Springer Nature publisher full HTML inspected.
modernSources.originResult: The study addresses distal tendon footprints, not tibialis posterior origin.
modernSources.insertionResult: Main navicular insertion was present in 41/41 specimens, with additional distal tendon footprints; supports distal complexity but not a project-mesh triangle boundary.

comparisonPolicy: Gray is retained as the historical source summary. Modern papers are compared field by field and only for what their own methods/results directly examined; background citation is not counted as a measured result.
